newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to look at banks' credit card, auto loans.
newsitem.headline: Manila to look at banks' credit card, auto loans.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank is examining banks' exposure to credit card and auto loans to ensure the banking industry stays healthy, Central Bank director Andres Rustia said on Tuesday.

"We would like to do our own survey. It's one way of dealing with any potential problem on a proactive way," Rustia told Reuters in a telephone interview. However, he said the examination was not triggered by any specific issues.
He said he expects to submit a report to the Monetary Board in two months' time and come out with the policy implications of such a study.
"We want to find out what's happening in those areas considering that other countries have been giving their own analysis in those sectors," he said.
Consumer lending has been viewed as a more risky area because of the absence of collateral.

Banks in the Philippines have been locked in intense competition for consumer loans amid a surge in retail spending within a fast-expanding economy. The industry has also sought to diversify its revenue sources as margins on corporate business shrink.
